_comment: well collision proxy (Blender frame, Z up; ws = 2.639 world m per raw unit; the mesh base sits at raw z -0.252). The round stone ring as ONE octagonal prism (centre from the measured ring bounds, radius hugging the stones' outer faces, top at the rim z 0.12 raw = ~0.98 m world) - an 8-gon hull is tight at the diagonals where the old axis-aligned box was ~0.37 m world fat. The A-frame roof posts, crank arm and roof are dropped (thin/overhang). Base extends below terrain. Roof: two wedges for the little A-frame so a jump at the well bonks the visible roof instead of passing the head through it (eave underside ~1.73 m world clears a walking capsule hugging the ring). The ring stops at the REAL rim (z 0.12 raw): the 0.1.48 fill to the roof underside is gone - the old rim pin was against the flat prism bottom of a roof WEDGE, and the roof is now sloped SLABS whose tilted undersides shed a jumping capsule sideways (a pin needs opposing parallel surfaces). The open rim-to-eave window (~0.9 m) is far too short for the 1.8 m capsule to ever rest in; '_lowHeadroomOk: ring' records the audited exemption, proven by the wedge-scan tests.
